# STLACCESS — STL Scale Converter for 3D Printed Miniatures

> Browser-based tool that calculates resize percentages for scaling STL files between tabletop gaming systems. Free, no upload, no login. All math runs in your browser.

## Key pages

- [STL Scale Converter (homepage)](https://stlaccess.com/) — Main calculator: 15+ gaming scales, eye-level and top-of-head measurement
- [Scale Conversion Reference](https://stlaccess.com/reference) — 45+ verified conversion percentages with print-tested results and methodology article
- [Conversion FAQ](https://stlaccess.com/faq) — Answers about 28mm, 32mm, 1:35, 1:48, 1:56, 1:72, and 1:100 scales
- [Methodology](https://stlaccess.com/about) — 175cm human baseline, FDM test prints with digital calipers
- [All Tools](https://stlaccess.com/tools) — stlscale Engine, Personal Library, Scale Reference, Creator Badge
- [Game Systems](https://stlaccess.com/games) — Scale guides for 20+ tabletop games
- [Blog](https://stlaccess.com/blog) — Deep-dive articles on miniature scale, 3D printing, and conversion math
- [Privacy Policy](https://stlaccess.com/privacy) — No cookies, no tracking, no data collection
- [Contact](https://stlaccess.com/contact) — Report errors, request new scales, suggest features

## Common conversions (based on 175cm human baseline, eye-level measurement)

| From | To | Slicer % |
|------|----|----------|
| 28mm | 32mm | 114.3% |
| 28mm | 35mm | 125.0% |
| 28mm | 40mm | 142.9% |
| 28mm | 75mm | 267.9% |
| 32mm | 28mm | 87.5% |
| 32mm | 35mm | 109.4% |
| 32mm | 40mm | 125.0% |
| 32mm | 75mm | 234.4% |
| 35mm | 28mm | 80.0% |
| 35mm | 32mm | 91.4% |
| 35mm | 40mm | 114.3% |
| 40mm | 32mm | 80.0% |
| 1:35 | 32mm | 64.0% |
| 1:48 | 32mm | 87.8% |
| 1:56 | 32mm | 102.4% |
| 1:35 | 1:56 | 62.5% |
| 1:72 | 32mm | 50.8% |
| 1:100 | 32mm | 36.0% |

## How it works

1. The user selects a source scale (e.g. 28mm) and target scale (e.g. 32mm)
2. The calculator divides the target human height by the source human height to get a percentage
3. The user enters that percentage in their slicer (PrusaSlicer, Cura, Chitubox, Lychee, Bambu Studio)
4. The STL scales proportionally in the slicer

## Methodology

- Human baseline: 175cm (standard reference height used by most miniature manufacturers)
- Measurement methods: "eye level" (top of eyes, ~167cm) and "top of head" (~175cm)
- All percentages verified with FDM test prints on a Bambu Lab A1 Mini
- Digital caliper measurements at 0.01mm precision
- No assumptions about manufacturer intent — measurements are empirical

## About

STLACCESS is a free, independent project by kitsorix (https://github.com/kitsorix-official). All percentages are calculated from a 175cm human baseline and verified with FDM test prints and digital calipers. The site has no backend, no tracking, no accounts — everything runs in your browser. Built with Astro. Source code on GitHub.
